I really wanted to enjoy WebFishing 
the core idea is relaxing and quite charming. The atmosphere is nice, and the general gameplay loop of fishing and exploring feels like something I could easily sink hours into.

However, on my system (AMD Radeon RX 9070), the game is unfortunately not playable in its current state.

There are severe graphical issues: white, noisy artifacts appear on surfaces and constantly flicker depending on camera movement. Each frame seems to produce different visual errors, which makes the image unstable and very distracting. Standing still already shows the issue, but moving the camera makes it significantly worse.

I tried multiple fixes without success:

* disabling all AMD Adrenalin features (Anti-Lag, Sharpening, Sync, etc.)
* limiting FPS
* changing in-game graphics settings (anti-aliasing, resolution scale, texture quality)
* testing different rendering setups and post-processing (ReShade)

Nothing resolved the problem, which suggests a deeper rendering or shader issue, possibly related to texture sampling or mipmapping on newer GPUs.

It’s a shame, because the game itself seems genuinely enjoyable.
But until this graphical issue is addressed, I cannot recommend it on newer AMD hardware.
Horrendous flickering textures cannot find a fix

This game is incompatible with newer AMD drivers. When looking and/or moving around the map the textures flicker to white pixel lines/shapes and back rapidly. Even when you stop moving the white textures will remain in that spot until you move again. From researching, the only fix is to revert your adrenaline version and clearing the shaders cache, but if we did that newer games couldn't be run. This is not an AMD issue but a poorly optimized game. Which is such a shame, I was looking forward to playing this game, but flashing textures make it unplayable, in my opinion.

You get what you pay for. For just a measely five dollars, you get a cutesy fishing game for furries, which comes with mods support (if you download GDWeave) and a few things to do aside from JUST fishing and talking. However, be aware that the game has some unpatched exploits, and only mods seem to fix them at this time. The developer is not coming back.

Buy this at your own discretion. If you're willing to buy it just to try it, and think you'll have a blast, do it! cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players overlook missing cloud support and halted updates while pursuing rare fish collections.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game does not support Steam Cloud saves, requiring manual backups when reinstalling or changing operating systems.

citations.review_text:
Even with the peak and drama of this game being far from gone, this game knows how to calm you down after a long day. Sure the servers aren't that populated anymore but the people that are still there are the kindest people I have met online in a while. The gameplay is simple but that's the best part, it's easy to understand and there is no requirement to learn complex mechanics in order to fully "finish" the game.

The only negative I can give is that Webfishing does not use Steam Cloud so make sure to back up your save file if you are swapping or reinstalling an OS. If you don't know where it's stored then a quick search should give you the answer whether you are on Windows or Linux.

If you are looking for a game that allows you to spend an hour de-stressing while watching a Youtube video on the side then this game is perfect for you.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that catching the remaining rare fish for complete journal or achievement completion involves a lengthy RNG-heavy grind.

citations.review_text:
Such a cute game with an amazing gameplay loop! The community is also so kind, helpful, and funny which makes it even more fun to play! It's really sad what happened to the dev of this game... with updates this game could have really been so much more not only in terms of gameplay but a bigger player base as well. Regardless I still have no regrets buying this game and can't wait to finish 100% clearing it :)

Edit: Wow i wrote this review 63 hours in...catching i think most of the fish outside the alpha ones and if you can believe it, took me like 80 more hours to get the rest of the fish haha. No regrets though...the grind was so much fun! Whether that was fishing with friends from the game, friends in a discord call, or just watching shows/ streams. I'll never forget all the time it took hunting the alphas ESPECIALLY my last fish...that dang alpha koi fish that might have been more than half of the time of the rest of the alphas combined xD. Super fun game though, i'll probably come back from time to time when I just want to chill and wind down.

Webfishing is a game that in my opinion ended up being both underrated and overrated all at once. While I think it definitely deserved the praise it got during its peak popularity, I think a lot of people sleep on the fact that, at its core, webfishing is an extremely solid experience- even now, a year+ later.

It's a great way to socialize, even if you usually struggle with social interactions. Webfishing makes it easy to make friends, and even easier to hang out with already existing ones. That being said, webfishing is also a wonderful experience to play solo. I experienced both ends of it while 100%'ing it and can with my full chest say that neither one is a superior experience. They both have their charm and the game could easily appeal to you regardless of if your playstyle is to be silly with your mates, or if you want a serious solo completionist experience. 

Webfishing, aside from catch rates that can be rightout infuriating at times (despite being sheer RNG, I know, I just- like everyone else playing this game, am salty some fish took stupidly long to catch), is extremely soothing and cozy. With nice timeless graphics, easy to grasp mechanics and a collectors book that is both big enough to be challanging, while being small enough to feel do-able. 

This game allows you to have upbeat fun and yap people's ears off, unwind and take a chill pill, or sulk and cope with things outside of your control that might be going on in your life, and as such, I can highly recommend it to anyone that might be considering or hesitant to buy it.

At worst, you find the game tideous and don't play more than a few hours, at best? You make memories with people that will stick with you, get an outlet, and a way to escape the short attention span feeding nonsense that is today's society. If you're hesitant, take the plunge! I promise you, you won't regret it.

58/10. Even with the dev abandoning it, it's still highly worth buying.

The game is fun! Expect a long grind to get EVERY fish, but it's very cozy and fun for more idle play! I usually played alone, but had plenty of sessions with my friends and community. Plenty of upgrades and cosmetics to keep the initial grind exciting and new. Hackers do run rampant, forcing their way into your lobbies, but I treat them like lil forest creatures. They're all pretty nice, and typically very helpful with tips and tricks. 

Sunk Cost Fallacy destroyed me with this one. I caught all but one fish on one rarity within 90 hours of gameplay... Probably sooner. It took my unlucky @$$ about 100+ hours to get my final fish, an alpha golden bass.

I was ready to sacrifice my first born, dance in a mushroom circle, I would've done anything to get this fish. The dopamine rush I got when I finally caught it made the struggle worth it. After almost 200 hours, and all achievements acquired, I can safely say:

10/10, would play again.

Fun game and a good community overall. You’ll meet a few weirdos, but that’s part of the experience.

If you’re the kind of person who needs to catch every fish in every variety, good luck. What starts as relaxing turns into a full mental breakdown over one fish :)

Great game. Bad for my sanity

Works well as a chatroom game, but the fishing mechanic is simplistic and gets old quickly. If you have the mental illness of needing to 100% every game, just be aware you are getting yourself into a 150-200 hour RNG fest.
